newsitem.title: USA: Bond impairment ruling in Ill. park case delayed.
newsitem.headline: Bond impairment ruling in Ill. park case delayed.

text.p: A DuPage County, Ill., Circuit Court judge on Wednesday delayed a decision on whether his ruling in a tax case would impair a park district's contract with bondholders.
Judge John Darrah said would take the matter under advisement until January, when he would rule on the matter involving the Lisle Park District.

The judge's decision came despite arguments by attorney's for business owners that brought the lawsuit against the county tax collector that no contracts were impaired by Darrah's April ruling because the bonds were paid.

Last month Darrah opened the door the impairment issue by giving attorneys representing the county and park districts time to brief their contention that his April ruling would unconstitutionally impair contracts with holders of the park district's debt.

Darrah in April ruled that property taxes used by the park district to pay off general obligation debt issued for the retirement of approximately $6 million of installment contracts and alternate bonds were subject to limitations under a 1991 state tax cap law.

That law subjected park districts and other local governments in five suburban Chicago counties to an annual limit in property tax collection increases of five percent or the rate of inflation, whichever is less. Any increase in taxes over that limite requires voter approval under the law.
Darrah ruled that all taxes levied in excess of the limit were illegal and void and that plaintiffs were entitled to a refund.
Because Lisle Park District was used a test case in the matter Darrah's ruling would affect other park districts that issued similar kinds of debt, according to attorneys.

But on Wednesday, Darrah expressed concern that some of the other park districts may suffer greater financial consequences as a result of his ruling than the Lisle district. And he raised the possibility that each park district's case might have to be tried separately.

Attorneys for the county also presented an affidavit from LaSalle Bank that said the bank holds $2.3 million of park district installment contracts and would not have bought the contracts if its agreement with the park districts could be impaired by the court, according to David Audley, an attorney at Chapman & Cutler, who is acting as a special assistant DuPage County state's attorney in the matter.

Court filings by defense attorneys claimed that Lisle Park District's contract with installment contract holders would be unconstitutionally impaired by Darrah's April ruling whether or not there is a default. That is because the district's pledge to issue GO debt to pay them off would be impaired. The filings also claimed that GO debt sold to pay off alternate bonds was statutorily authorized and exempted from the tax cap law.
